fieldValues.title: The batch seam refuses instead of lying about rollback
fieldValues.summary: RepositoryStore's begin_batch/commit_batch/abort_batch had no-op defaults, so FileStore and MemoryStore silently inherited a rollback guarantee neither can keep. Removed the defaults (every implementor must answer explicitly), added supports_batch_rollback(), and made abort_batch return Err(BatchSeamUnsupported) on both stores instead of claiming success. Corrected the false ADR-021 comments in migrate_carrier and its siblings, and wired rfc038_storage_migration_service's existing hardcoded refusal to the new real capability check.
fieldValues.body: Item 3 of #1015 ("every batch caller refuses up front before its first write") was implemented fully only for rfc038_storage_migration_service (already precedented, zero behavior change). It was NOT applied to migrate_carrier or its sibling migrations (discovery-query-cutover, composition-cutover, migrate_identity_service), because: neither FileStore nor MemoryStore has ever supported real rollback (JsonStore, which the issue assumed still existed with a real override, was actually retired in #783 Phase 4); migrate_carrier's ~10 existing tests and its production CLI path run almost entirely through .srsj/MemVfs-backed sessions, which are safe via a separate mechanism (the projection boundary only flushes to a real file on success, see repository_portability::srsj_partial_import_is_never_projected_to_the_file), not via the batch seam; and supports_batch_rollback() as a store-type-level capability cannot honestly distinguish safe-because-session-backed from risky-because-on-disk for the same FileStore struct. Applying the refusal unconditionally would have broken ~10 currently-passing tests and disabled these migrations in production with no escape hatch. Filed srs-rust#1018 as the follow-up (add an allow_non_atomic-style opt-in mirroring rfc038_storage_migration_service's already-shipped pattern).
